target_state.target: Frank v0.1 / self.root on accepted Hostinger Ubuntu VPS

selected_frontier.reason: Current main has merged SQLite V6 source-byte pins and loader/path hardening, while productive installation, restart/recovery, rollback/downgrade/library-swap and semantic-lineage acceptance remain open. The current launcher hashes six guard source pathnames and later execs Python, which reopens those pathnames during import.
duplicate_avoidance: PR #467 already covers mapped SQLite inode/path replacement after DSO load
PR #513 already covers stale parallel root-owned ProductStart identity and explicitly leaves anti-rollback freshness open
This run tests a distinct pre-Python source-chain coherence window: verified pathname bytes can change between shell hash and Python import during a legitimate multi-object release update

observed_reality.launcher_behavior: For each V6->V1 guard pathname, verify ownership/link shape and SHA-256 using pathname tools, then later exec /usr/bin/python3 -I -S on the V6 guard pathname. V6 and lower guards import sibling source files by pathname.
observed_reality.current_merged_scope: V6-to-V1 source release bytes are pinned; productive install/root anchor/actual Frank process mapping/restart/recovery/rollback/downgrade/library-swap remain open.

hypothesis: Exact guard SHA-256 checks performed before Python exec are sufficient to prove that Python later executes/imports those same source bytes.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Because the launcher hashes by pathname and Python later reopens by pathname, an atomic replacement after the hash check can produce a different executable source view even though the precheck passed. Root-only path ownership blocks an unprivileged caller but does not eliminate legitimate root deployment/update races, which are release-correctness relevant during start/restart/upgrade.

go_out_of_box.name: PIN_THEN_SWAP_GUARD_PATH_REOPEN
go_out_of_box.method: In a disposable local directory, write pinned guard bytes and record their SHA-256. Baseline: hash then execute the same path unchanged. Treatment: restore pinned bytes, verify the same expected hash, atomically os.replace() a different source file over the pathname, then execute that pathname with Python.
go_out_of_box.scope: Demonstrates the generic pathname hash->reopen mechanism. It is not a claim that an unprivileged Frank caller can mutate root-owned production guards, and it does not prove that such a race has occurred on Hostinger.

external_primary_evidence.finding: WAL-reset bug is documented through 3.51.2 and fixed in 3.51.3 and later.
3.53.4 is in the fixed lineage and exposes the exact project-pinned SQLITE_SOURCE_ID.

external_primary_evidence.source: GNU C Library Dynamic Linker Hardening
external_primary_evidence.finding: glibc warns against in-place updates of active program/shared-object files and warns that multi-object updates can let concurrently starting processes observe inconsistent combinations of old and new objects.

architecture_delta.supported_change: Final ProductStart/storage acceptance must prove an atomic or otherwise stable executable release view across the shell hash -> Python exec -> sibling import window. Exact pathname hashes are necessary but not sufficient if a privileged deployment update can replace release files between verification and import.
candidate_repair_realities: Immutable/content-addressed release directories that are never modified in place, with atomic whole-release activation and old-release retention for already-starting processes
Stable opened-file/inode or sealed-object execution/import design for the complete guard chain
A machine-checked deployment protocol that excludes concurrent release mutation during ProductStart admission and proves rollback/downgrade behavior
architecture_delta.strongest_counter_reality: If the accepted production deployment contract already proves that the root-owned guard directory is immutable for the entire admission interval and release activation is atomic, the generic counterworld may be unreachable in production; this must be demonstrated rather than inferred from root ownership.
architecture_delta.next_discriminating_test: On an exact-current candidate release tree, start a controlled ProductStart admission while a privileged test updater attempts an atomic whole-file replacement between source pin verification and Python import. Require either stable execution of the pinned release or deterministic fail-closed denial; never admit a mixed release.
architecture_delta.rollback: No product repair was merged by this research run. Preserve current V6 source pins; add the coherence gate as a new obligation rather than weakening existing checks.

coordination.note: PR #513 remains draft/open and its documented target run did not complete. Fresh-current recomposition should include this release-coherence obligation instead of treating #513 as current target PASS.

nonclaims: No claim that SQLite 3.53.4 itself is vulnerable to the WAL-reset bug
No claim of root compromise or unprivileged privilege escalation
next_frontier: Recompose ProductStart identity/current source-chain work on fresh main and add a deterministic mixed-release coherence gate
Then execute clean start/restart plus rollback/downgrade/library-swap and semantic-lineage recovery acceptance
